row.evidence: Fly.io's SSO docs say it 'supports Google and GitHub as Identity Providers' for an org-level sign-in requirement, members are invited by email and removed through the dashboard, and no SCIM or SAML is documented anywhere in its docs or pricing.
row.notes: New row. None by absence. Pricing is usage-based (Pay As You Go, no platform fee) with optional support plans (Standard $29/mo, Premium $199/mo, Enterprise from $2,500/mo, monthly), so per-user fields are null. 'SSO' is a Google hosted-domain or GitHub org requirement, which is social-style sign-in and does not count as SAML/OIDC SSO, so sso_plan is null. Org roles are only Member and Admin. No public member-management API: the Machines REST API covers apps and machines, and invites/removals are via the dashboard or flyctl.

plans.name: Pay As You Go
plans.price_text: No monthly platform fee; usage-based resource pricing
plans.notes: SSO is a Google Workspace hosted-domain or GitHub organization requirement, not SAML/OIDC with the customer's own IdP.

scim.notes: No SCIM, SAML or IdP provisioning is mentioned in the Fly.io docs index (llms.txt), security section or pricing.

user_api.notes: The documented public API (Machines REST API) covers apps, machines, volumes, certificates and tokens, not org members. Member invite/remove is documented only as flyctl commands (fly orgs invite, fly orgs remove).

google.notes: Google sign-in can be required per org by hosted domain (OAuth-style, not SAML). No provisioning.

fallbacks.notes: Members are invited by email (dashboard or flyctl) and removed manually; Fly's offboarding guide lists manual token, WireGuard and secret clean-up.
